text:
sam: quick handoff — overnight embed autoscaler oscillation triggered several pages in eu-west, filing a concise summary so next shift can pick up. TL;DR: customer-facing p95 spike + intermittent 502/503 for a subset of requests; primary mitigations applied, still monitoring.

sam: timeline: 02:15 UTC alert (pagerbot) -> 02:20 started mitigation (scale up + pinned variant) -> 02:32 rollback autoscaler tweak -> 02:40 confirmed error rate falling.

pagerbot: [pager] EMBED_POOL_THROTTLE eu-west - 02:15 UTC - p95 tokens latency > 8s, errors spike to 6% (threshold 1%).

neha: who was primary on that pager?

sam: I was primary until 03:00 when alex took the bridge. alex: can you add anything?

alex: jumped on at ~02:22. Root cause looks like a feedback loop: autoscaler reduced replicas during a short low-QPS window, prefix/KV eviction then caused heavy regen when burst returned. Evictions caused CPU+VRAM transient pressure -> higher tail latency and 502s.

alex: actions taken:
- temporarily pinned embeddings pool to 6 replicas (was autoscale 1-8).
- enabled model fallback for heavy requests to smaller-quantized variant (model-v2-q4f).
- increased KV cache retention for eu-west (ramp from 30s -> 5m) via runtime toggle.

sam: also ran the quick check script: 
```bash
# quick health checks I ran
/rise run health embed-pool eu-west
curl -sS https://metrics.internal/recent?pool=embed-eu | jq .p95
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot executed a safe config toggle: autoscaler.enabled=false on service embed-eu at 02:25 UTC (change-id: cfg-2026-4242).

deploy-bot: canary toggles applied, metrics show drop in 5xxs after 02:36 UTC.

neha: current customer impact? which clients saw errors?

alex: subset of high-concurrency customers in eu-west (customer-ids: cust-984, cust-1023, cust-2107). We sent an incident banner to affected customers (ops->support) at 02:45. Customer-facing latency reduced to baseline by ~02:50.

sam: monitoring: Alerts re-armed but suppressed while we confirm stability. Key metrics to watch: embed-pool p95, 5xx rate, kv-evicts/s, cpu-utilization on embed nodes. I left three dashboards pinned in the runbook.

neha: coverage: I'm primary for the 03:00-11:00 UTC window, alex is secondary until 07:00 then switches to engineering on-call rotation. Confirming: alex you're secondary?

alex: yes I'm secondary until 07:00. After that handoff note for next oncall: re-enable autoscaler only after we validate mem/evict pattern under synthetic bursts.

sam: outstanding next steps (short):
- PROV-7592 (sam): follow-up ticket to add hysteresis to embeddings autoscaler (min replicas floor + burst hold) — started, assigned to infra-ml.
- PROV-7593 (alex): postmortem skeleton + short RCA, target due EOD.
- PROV-7594 (neha): run extended soak test with synthetic burst in eu-west (3h) and share results.
- Ops: leave autoscaler.disabled toggle in place until soak confirms, do not change replica count manually except if instructed by oncall lead.

neha: i'll kick off soak at 04:10 UTC and drop results in this thread. Will also add a small perf test to confirm fallback model quality impact.

alex: runbook pointers: https://internal/runbooks/embed-eviction and https://internal/ops/playbooks/autoscaler-hysteresis — both links have checklist for quick mitigate and how to revert the fallback model.

sam: communication: support notified; CSM pinged for high-entropy customers. No public outage page needed (we classified as degraded partial impact).

neha: risk notes: leaving autoscaler off increases cost temporarily; document cost delta in the follow-up ticket. Also watch for longer-term cache growth if we keep retention at 5m.

sam: final status for handoff: mitigations applied, 5xxs trending down to baseline, autoscaler disabled for now, soak test running, oncall coverage: neha primary (03:00-11:00 UTC), alex secondary until 07:00. Next update ETA 05:00 UTC or earlier if regression.

alex: +1, i'll stay on watch and will escalate to infra if evictions spike again.

neha: noted. Thanks all — picking up. :white_check_mark:
